_comment: actual-clean.json with ONE injected defect per diff category (a)-(i). Every departure from the clean
mirror is marked `INJECTED (x)` below, and `manifest.json` names the finding each one must produce.
The self-check asserts SET EQUALITY both ways, so a defect that stops being reported fails by name,
and a finding the diff invents fails too.
Three injections cascade on purpose, and the manifest lists every consequence rather than only the
headline: the grey neutral/900 is both a stale value (c) AND two AA failures (g), and a component the
file does not have is both a missing component (f) AND its binding going unbound (a). A cascade the
manifest did not list would fail as an EXTRA — which is the point. The two arms are independent, and
the fixture proves it by requiring both to fire.
Two injections are OMISSIONS and so have no marker to carry — read them against actual-clean.json:
(f) `gadget` is gone from `structure`, and its one binding is gone from `bindings`
(f) `fix/color/text/secondary` is gone from `variables` — the missing-variable path, which is the
highest-consequence finding in the report and the one an omission-shaped defect would leave
unproven
(i) the `Grid / xs` grid style is gone from `styles` — the same omission shape one level in, and the
one that proves a whole style going missing is not mistaken for a library-consumed one
`libraryConsumed` is carried here UNCHANGED from the clean mirror, and that is load-bearing rather than
copied for tidiness: every arm's suppression has to hold while OTHER arms are firing. Drop it and the
`shared` collection, `fix/shared/brand/500` and `body/lg/default` each surface as an extra finding — a
diff that reports real defects and phantom ones alongside them is not one anybody can act on.

fix/color/icon/primary._injected: (d) mode-coverage — the `dark` mode the engine emits is missing

fix/core/palette/neutral/900._injected: (c) value-match, and (g) contrast ×2 — hand-nudged from rgba(26,26,26,1) to a mid grey, which both drifts from the emitted value and drops light-mode text below 4.5:1

fix/size/md/height._injected: (e) scope-type — scopes widened to ALL_SCOPES, so the variable is offered where it should not be. The VALUE is untouched, which is what keeps this a scope finding and not a value one.

fix/opacity/veil._injected: (e) scope-type — wrong resolvedType. Nothing binds this variable and no contract measures it, so the finding cannot be a side effect of another arm.

widget|size=md, state=rest|/|fills._injected: (a) binding-presence — a raw literal where the engine binds fix/color/background/primary

widget|size=md, state=rest|/label|fills._injected: (b) binding-target — bound to the ICON role where the engine binds the TEXT role, the exact confusion the category exists for

widget|size=md, state=rest|/label|textSt._injected: (a) binding-presence — a VARIABLE where the engine binds a text STYLE. A different Figma API, not a wrong value, so it must be reported as a presence failure and never as a target one: `fix/color/text/primary` is not a plausible replacement for `body/md/default`, and a target finding would invite a fix that cannot work.

widget|size=md, state=rest|/caption|font._injected: (a) binding-presence, the DETACHED shape — `/caption textStyle` is gone from this file, but all three of the style's font fields are still here. So the node reads correct on every property and has lost the style LINK. A diff that only looked for a wrong value would call this clean.

widget|size=md, state=rest|/caption|fill._injected: (a) binding-presence, the RAW LITERAL WHOSE VARIABLE THIS FILE DOES NOT HAVE — the un-rebindable twin of `/|fills` above, and the pair is the whole safe/unsafe boundary of the P2 fix loop (#1553 P2, fix.ts). The two findings are the same shape in the report: a hex where a variable belongs. Only one is safely fixable, because `fix/color/background/primary` is in this file and `fix/color/text/secondary` is the variable the (f) omission took out — so a rebind here has nothing to bind TO, and emitting one would be a fix that cannot run. Both halves in one file for the same reason the strokeWeight lenience is proven working and failing in one file.

widget|size=md, state=hover|/|strokeTopW._injected: (b) binding-target, the per-side DISAGREEMENT — the engine binds one uniform strokeWeight and this member's left/right sides point somewhere else. The `rest` member above keeps all four agreeing, so the same lenience is proven working and failing in one file.

text|body/md/default._injected: (i) style-definition, the UNIT difference — the engine bakes a unitless multiplier as PERCENT and this style carries 21px, which is 150% of 14 and therefore identical in this mode and wrong in every other one. Reported, deliberately, and not normalized away: a pixel line height has lost exactly the mode-invariance the bake exists to provide (#1356).
text|body/md/default.name: body/md/default

text|caption/md/default._injected: (i) style-definition, and it CASCADES on purpose — `fontStyle` is detached to the literal 'Bold' where the engine binds a variable, which is both a raw value where a binding was planned AND, read through the weight table, a 700 where the engine planned 400. Two findings on one subject, because a detached font style really is both things at once. Nothing else here checks the weight: it is the only property the engine plans that Figma does not have.
text|caption/md/default.name: caption/md/default

text|label/sm/default._injected: (i) style-definition, the WRONG VARIABLE — `fontSize` is bound to a height variable rather than the font-size one. Bound, so a scan that only asked whether a property was variable-bound would call it correct, and the label renders at 40px. The highest-consequence interior defect after a style going missing outright, and the one a size-vs-height name confusion produces in practice.
text|label/sm/default.name: label/sm/default

effect|shadow/sm._injected: (i) style-definition — the second layer's y offset moved from 2 to 6. One field of one layer of a two-layer shadow: a diff that compared whole effect arrays, or only their count, would miss it.
effect|shadow/sm.name: shadow/sm

paint|gradient/brand._injected: (i) style-definition — the end stop is a flat colour where the engine binds a palette variable. The colour is the RIGHT one, so the gradient looks correct and will not follow the palette when it moves: #1387 at the style interior, and the reason a style property is modelled as variable-or-value rather than flattened to its resolved colour.
paint|gradient/brand.name: gradient/brand

text|designer/scratch._injected: (i) style-definition, the EXTRA — a local style the engine plans nowhere. Low severity by design: an extra style is a housekeeping question, not a broken contract, and reporting it at the same weight as a missing one would bury the missing one.
text|designer/scratch.name: designer/scratch
